hook.say: North America's ten highest mountains, ranked. Three of them are volcanoes in Mexico!

outro.say: Which one surprised you? Comment below!

items.name: Mount Bona
items.say: Number ten: Mount Bona, an ice-covered volcano. 16550 feet.
items.cap: Number ten: Mount Bona, an ice-covered volcano. 16,550 feet.

items.name: King Peak
items.say: Nine: King Peak, Mount Logan's little brother. 16972 feet.
items.cap: Nine: King Peak, Mount Logan's little brother. 16,972 feet.

items.name: Iztaccíhuatl
items.say: Eight: Ista-seewattle, the Sleeping Woman. 17159 feet.
items.cap: Eight: Iztaccíhuatl, the Sleeping Woman. 17,159 feet.

items.name: Mount Lucania
items.say: Seven: Mount Loo-kaynia, deep in the Yukon wild. 17257 feet.
items.cap: Seven: Mount Lucania, deep in the Yukon wild. 17,257 feet.

items.name: Mount Foraker
items.say: Six: Mount Forakker, Denali's neighbor. 17400 feet.
items.cap: Six: Mount Foraker, Denali's neighbor. 17,400 feet.

items.name: Popocatépetl
items.say: Five: Popo-catepettle, an active volcano near Mexico City. 17749 feet.
items.cap: Five: Popocatépetl, an active volcano near Mexico City. 17,749 feet.

items.name: Mt. Saint Elias
items.say: Four: Mount Saint Elias, on the Alaska Yukon border. 18009 feet.
items.cap: Four: Mt. Saint Elias, on the Alaska Yukon border. 18,009 feet.

items.name: Pico de Orizaba
items.say: Three: Peeko day Oree-sahba, North America's highest volcano. 18491 feet.
items.cap: Three: Pico de Orizaba, North America's highest volcano. 18,491 feet.

items.name: Mount Logan
items.say: Two: Mount Logan, the roof of Canada. 19551 feet.
items.cap: Two: Mount Logan, the roof of Canada. 19,551 feet.

items.name: Denali
items.say: And number one: Denali! 20310 feet, the roof of North America.
items.cap: And number one: Denali! 20,310 feet, the roof of North America.
